question_v1.title: Does structured new-case preparation reduce avoidable callbacks?
question_v1.question: For new referrals to the fictional service, is documented identity review, patient-goal recording and acknowledged handoff associated with fewer preparation callbacks?
question_v1.scope: Operational case-preparation workflow of the fictional AML service.
question_v1.intended_use: Inform a departmental preparation protocol and handoff SOP. Not for individual treatment recommendations.

appraisal_v1.population: Invented adult new-case referrals (as reported in the synthetic note)
appraisal_v1.intervention: Structured preparation packet with identity review and acknowledged handoff
appraisal_v1.outcome: Callbacks for missing information; completed handoffs
appraisal_v1.findings: The synthetic note reports fewer callbacks with documented identity review and more completed handoffs when explicitly accepted.
appraisal_v1.uncertainty: Direction and size of any effect are unknown.
appraisal_v1.limitations: Invented single-site data, no comparison group, no clinical outcomes.

question_v2.title: Should caregiver contact be confirmed before handoff?
question_v2.question: Does confirming a caregiver contact before handoff reduce same-day delays?
question_v2.scope: Handoff step of the fictional preparation pathway.
question_v2.intended_use: Consider a revision of the departmental preparation protocol.

appraisal_v2.findings: The synthetic note reports fewer same-day delays with a confirmed contact.
appraisal_v2.limitations: Invented data; not evidence for any clinical decision.
